question.leadin: This 18th century ruler issued a decree that created the Smolny [SMOHL-nee] Institute of Noble Maidens, the first public European learning institution for girls.
question.text: Name this Russian empress, whose collaboration with many Enlightenment thinkers earned her the nickname "Enlightened Despot."
question.clue: Victories at the Chesma, Iasi, and Ochakov led to favorable terms in the Treaty of Jassy that expanded this ruler's empire.

swap.text: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.
swap.clue: Prince Potemkin had a close relationship with its Catherine the Great.

question.leadin: In 1978, Georgi Markov died after a ricin-filled pellet was injected into his thigh, probably by an umbrella gun.
question.text: The pellet was allegedly designed by this security agency, led at the time by Yuri Andropov.
question.clue: It evolved from earlier organizations, such as Cheka, but came directly from the NKVD, which had been led by Levrenty Beria.

swap.text: The "Secret Speech" was given by this successor to Stalin. During a meeting with the United Nations, this leader allegedly banged his shoe on a table in protest.
swap.clue: This leader's name was combined with the word for "slum" to name a set of buildings that replaced the kommunalka; he is thus the namesake of those ubiquitous, five-story block apartments.

question.text: During the Time of Troubles, a group of three individuals were given this collective name after they all claimed to be the youngest son of Ivan the Terrible.
question.clue: This figures who marched from the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth into Moscow, where their Cossack supporters installed them as tsars.

swap.text: The port of Sevastopol was later besieged in this 1850s war, which was fought over a peninsula on the Black Sea.
swap.clue: During this conflict, foggy conditions allowed for reinforcements that led to the Russian defeat at the Battle of Inkerman.

question.text: This member of the Rurikids reconquered Novgorod after fleeing his brother and converted the Rus to Christianity. The politician who wrote the pamphlet What Is To Be Done? shares his first name.
question.clue: In 988, this father of Yaroslav the Wise married Anna Porphyrogenita ], the sister of Basil the Bulgar Slayer, confirming an alliance with the Byzantines and formalizing this man's conversion to Christianity.

swap.leadin: -answer the following about important months in European history.
swap.text: During this month in 1905, Nicholas II issued a manifesto promising basic civil rights and the creation of the Duma. Trotsky and Lenin led a 1917 revolution in this month that established the Soviet government of Russia.
swap.clue: Israel fought Egypt and Syria in the Yom Kippur War during this month.

question.leadin: Answer the following about tank photographs.
question.text: A series of photographs depict this leader giving a speech while atop a tank in front of a "White House". He was the first Russian president in the post-Soviet Union era.
question.clue: This man faced the Chechen War and returned the KAL 007 black box.

swap.text: He married Zoe Paleologus, the niece of Constantine XI, and ordered Vladimir Gusev to compile his legal reforms in the Sudebnik. He also ended the tribute to Khan Ahmed and won a major victory at Ugra. For 15 points, name this son of Vasily II, the first man to claim the title "Grand Duke of all Russians" and namesake of a vicious grandson.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan III of Russia [or Ivan the Great; or Ivan III Vasilevich]
swap.clue: The Great Stand on the Ugra took place following this ruler's refusal to pay tribute to Akhmat Khan, a move symbolizing the end of the Tatar yoke on Moscow.

question.text: More substantially, Catherine founded this educational establishment, the first for women in Russia. Its building would house the Bolshevik headquarters during the October Revolution.

swap.text: The Russians under Alexander Menshikov won this 1709 battle near the namesake Ukrainian city. Fleeing Swedish troops under Adam Lewenhaupt surrendered at Perevolochna shortly after this battle.
swap.clue: The siege precipitating it was the first phase of one side's plan to strike at the other's capital, a plan that was bolstered by the defection of Ivan Mazepa.

question.leadin: In principle, any resident of this city could ring a bell to summon its entire population to either its "Trade" or "Sophia" sides.
question.text: Name this mercantile city-state that housed the easternmost kontor of the Hanseatic League. This city's conquest by Muscovy after the 1471 Battle of Shelon led to the abolition of its veche ("VETCH-yeh") assembly.
question.answerHtml: Veliky Novgorod [or Novgorod Republic or Lord Novgorod the Great; reject “Nizhny Novgorod”]
question.clue: This city's St. Sophia Cathedral is home to the bones of Yaroslav the Wise.

swap.text: After he defeated a revolt by his uncle Peter III Aaron, Stephen the Great executed many members of this class who had supported his uncle. Nobility of this class were subjected to a "beard tax" in another country.
swap.clue: To undermine the influence of these people, a tsar introduced a system in which collegiate registrars were graded "K-14."

question.text: Historian James Billington links Fomenko's idea that Russia was the Mongol Empire to this socio-political movement, highlighting Russia's Asiatic identity. Aleksandr Dugin ("doo-GIN") leads a "neo-" version of this movement.

swap.text: In the 13th century, a pope with this name sent John of Montecorvino as a missionary to China and the Mongols. This was the given first name of the only English pope, Adrian IV, who was surnamed Breakspear.
swap.clue: Soldiers tried to replace a tsar of this name with his brother Konstantin in the Decembrist Revolt.

question.leadin: She was offered the throne by the Supreme Privy Council on the death of Peter II.
question.text: Name this Russian empress whose reign was dominated by Biron, Osterman, and Munnich, and who oversaw Russian participation in the War of the Polish Succession during her reign.
question.clue: After the Supreme Privy Council put this woman in power, she promptly abolished it.

swap.leadin: Name these advisors to Catherine the Great.
swap.text: This final lover and favorite of Catherine was of ignoble birth and irritated his courtiers by allowing his pet monkey to steal their hats. After being exiled from court by Tsar Paul following Catherine's death, he participated in the coup against Paul.

question.text: The first False Dmitri appeared during the reign of Boris Gudonov, the brother-in-law of this last tsar of the Rurik dynasty.

swap.leadin: Improbable accounts claim that a British spy hid himself in a pavilion where these two rulers met and became friends in the aftermath of a series of bloody battles including Friedland and Eylau.
swap.text: Name these two rulers, who reaffirmed their alliance a year later at the Congress of Erfurt.
swap.answerHtml: Alexander I AND Napoleon Bonaparte [prompt on partial answers for both, including Bonaparte]
swap.clue: One of these two leaders decided to curb the other's power after hearing that he had arrested the Duke of Enghien from Baden , his wife's home town.
